Fable-Opus-Unit: nts-t004/spike-c-thin-wrapper-cost
Fable-Opus-Timeout-Minutes: 60
Fable-Opus-Effort: high
Effort-Justification: This spike measures the true post-industrialization per-app cost — the number the owner's end-to-end-automation decision will be priced on — by running a never-completed app through the frozen React adapter via the thin-wrapper path with honest per-stage clocking; conflating authoring time with machine time or fudging a bounded outcome would misprice the whole next tranche.

## Goal

SPIKE C (T003 Judge package) in /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/versionless: measure the REAL amortized per-app cost after industrialization. Candidate: `react-shlink-web-client` (existing consented ingest at evidence/ingests/react-shlink-web-client/); fallback `react-sqlpad-v5-5-0`. UNCOUNTED spike evidence only — no matrix/coverage/corpus changes.

Do, clocking wall-time per stage and counting new TS lines as you go (the LEDGER of costs is the product of this spike):
1. LICENSE PRE-SCREEN (mandatory gate zero, T018-u1 method): license-text-at-pin MIT with recorded licenseSha256 at the exact pinned revision recorded in the existing ingest. If it fails, fall back to react-sqlpad-v5-5-0; if both fail, blocked (that is a finding).
2. COMPLETE THE INGEST if partial (double-fetch byte-identical archive at pin, sha256, parity — the established method; consent VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10, URLs recorded; offline after).
3. BASELINE: era cell per the app's own declarations; install; production build x2 byte-compared (the app is CRA/webpack-era React — record what it actually is).
4. MIGRATE under the FROZEN React adapter (composite 27741d9c — recompute before/after; zero frozen-subtree edits; a gap is a named finding, never a fix): operator/fixture flow, install, build x2 byte-compared.
5. WITNESS via the THIN-WRAPPER path ONLY: per-app wrapper <= ~120 lines over real-app-run.ts (the dejavu/fuxa pattern), generic witness-real-app schema, NO per-app module in packages/core/src/receipts (if one appears required, that IS the finding — record and stop witness work). 2+2 serialized passes with calibration (max 3 calibration rounds; overrun is itself the answer). Real interactions, settled anchors, locality, honest bounded outcome if surfaces are limited.
6. EVIDENCE to evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/: per-stage wall-clock ledger, new-TS-line count by file, outcomes (build digests, witness digests or bounded-outcome wording), capability firings observed (recorded only — no coverage regeneration), and the verdict: is ~3u/app credible post-industrialization? What remains manual and how long did each manual act take?

## File contract

- `evidence/ingests/react-shlink-web-client/**`
- `evidence/ingests/react-sqlpad-v5-5-0/**`
- `evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/**`
- `packages/cli/src/fixture/react-shlink-web-client-migration-run.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/fixture/react-sqlpad-v5-5-0-migration-run.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/witness/react-shlink-web-client-run.ts`
- `packages/cli/src/witness/react-sqlpad-v5-5-0-run.ts`
- `packages/cli/test/**`
- `docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/**`

## Forbidden moves

- ZERO frozen-subtree edits (freeze recompute == 27741d9c before/after). No per-app packages/core/src/receipts module (its necessity is a finding, not a task). No packages/cli/src/operator/* changes. No enterprise-report/capability-coverage/matrix regeneration. No parallel witness passes. Network only for the pinned acquisition/license reads under the consent ID. Strict TypeScript, magic-regexp, pathe, ufo. Do not commit or stage. Kill processes; leave nothing listening.

## Verification

```verify
pnpm exec tsc --noEmit
pnpm exec vp lint
pnpm exec vp test --project node
sh -c 'node -e "const v=require(\"./evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json\"); if(!v.stageLedger||!v.verdict) throw new Error(\"incomplete\"); console.log(\"thin-wrapper verdict:\", v.verdict.threeUnitsCredible, \"outcome:\", v.verdict.outcome)"'
sh -c 'for p in packages/frameworks/react packages/frameworks/angular packages/core/src/migrations packages/core/src/bundlers packages/core/src/analysis; do echo "$p $(git rev-parse HEAD:$p)"; done | shasum -a 256 | grep -q 27741d9c && echo FREEZE-INTACT'
```

## Blocked permission

If both candidates fail license-at-pin (bring the texts), the frozen adapter cannot carry the app (named gap = valuable finding, record and stop), a per-app receipts module appears required (record and stop witness), the 5h/3-round budget hits (partials are the answer), or verification fails twice, return status "blocked" with specifics in open_questions instead of improvising.

# Versionless contributor instructions

## Architecture

- Write every Versionless-owned executable source, test, script, and configuration file in strict TypeScript (`.ts` or `.tsx`). Declarative JSON and YAML are allowed.
- Do not add hand-maintained `.js`, `.mjs`, or `.cjs` files. Immutable legacy fixture source and generated `dist/` output are the only exceptions.
- Keep the repository as a pnpm workspace driven by the root `vite.config.ts` and Vite+ commands (`vp pack`, `vp fmt`, `vp lint`, and `vp test`).
- Keep framework-specific transforms behind framework adapters. React and Angular are the primary adapters, but core orchestration, policy, evidence, and receipt code must remain framework-neutral.

## Required utilities

- Use `magic-regexp` builders for every Versionless-owned regular expression. Do not introduce regular-expression literals or `new RegExp`. Prefer named, readable patterns and enable the `magic-regexp` Vite transform. An unavoidable third-party API boundary requires a comment explaining the exception.
- Use `pathe` for filesystem path parsing, joining, resolving, normalization, relative paths, extensions, and basenames. Do not import `node:path` or `path` directly.
- Use `ufo` for URL parsing, joining, resolving, normalization, encoding, and pathname/hash/query access. Do not hand-roll URL concatenation or use regular expressions for URL handling.
- These rules apply to implementation and tests. Do not rewrite immutable third-party legacy fixtures merely to conform to them.

## Enterprise and evidence boundaries

- Default to local and offline operation. Network access requires an explicit purpose-bound consent ID and durable evidence of the exact sources accessed.
- Never include payment data, credentials, tokens, host-specific absolute paths, usernames, or other sensitive material in generated evidence. Preserve unknown, stale, blocked, ambiguous, and not-tested states rather than strengthening claims.
- Generated receipts and trust artifacts establish reproducibility and hash integrity, not certification, legal compliance, signer authenticity, OS-wide isolation, or an unearned SLSA level.
- Keep real legacy corpus inputs immutable. Apply migrations in separate worktrees, prove browser behavior with Playwright, include a mutation-red/restoration proof, and preserve canonical receipt digests.

## Verification

- Run `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`, `pnpm exec vp fmt`, `pnpm exec vp lint`, `pnpm exec vp pack`, and `pnpm exec vp test --project node` after source changes.
- Run fixture and receipt verification offline after the one explicitly consented ingest step.
- Do not claim a migration, runtime, bundler, or compliance cell is supported until its build, browser journey, locality checks, artifacts, and receipt independently verify.

<!-- guessless-integration:begin -->

## Structural claims about JavaScript/TypeScript

Do not assert that you have found _all_ call sites, _every_ reference, or that a symbol is safe to
delete, unless you can show a guessless receipt for that exact claim. `grep` cannot see re-exports,
aliased imports, `export * from`, or property access through a namespace object, so "all" derived
from a text search is a guess.

To price a completeness claim:

    node /Users/jacksm5pro/dev/open-source/guessless/packages/cli/dist/cli.js query envelope.json

where `envelope.json` is `{"inputs": [{"path": "...", "source": "..."}], "request": {...}}`. The
answer is a receipt whose `state` is one of:

- `complete` — the result set is exhaustive. This is the only state that licenses the word "all".
- `partial` — plus a named `unresolved` site for every place the engine could not classify. Say the
  answer is partial and name the gaps.
- `refused` — the question was not answered. It supports no claim at all.

If you have no receipt, say which sites you checked instead of saying "all". A qualified answer is
always acceptable; an unpriced "all" is not.

<!-- guessless-integration:end -->

# Next Tranche Strategy

## Objective

Determine, with receipt-backed evidence, what Versionless needs most next — and the most robust strategies and testing that get there fastest — then put a decision-ready brief in front of the owner. The prior goal (`legacy-react-angular-production-readiness`, completed 2026-08-14 with `full_outcome_complete: true`) closed the 6/6+4/4 matrix, both frozen-adapter holdouts, and the enterprise claims surfaces. This goal decides and de-risks what comes next, against the owner's ~2026-08-17 start of a 300+ application fleet migration.

## Original Request

"Do goal prep to explore what we need the most next, along with the most robust strategies and testing that will get us there the fastest. At the end of the goal you will make the information apparent to me as to how to proceed."

## Intake Summary

- Input shape: `open_ended` (strategic; owner directed defaults + immediate execution under a 15m loop)
- Audience: the owner (adoption/fleet-migration decision maker) and Versionless maintainers
- Authority: `approved` (same local, non-destructive charter as the prior goal; consent ID `VL-LEGACY-CORPUS-2026-08-10` for any public MIT acquisition)
- Proof type: `decision` backed by `demo` evidence — the brief's top recommendations must be de-risked by executed spikes, not asserted
- Completion proof: an owner decision brief, committed and surfaced, in which every candidate direction carries evidence, the ranked recommendation carries at least one executed de-risk spike with receipts, and a final Judge maps the brief to its evidence with `full_outcome_complete: true`
- Likely misfire: (a) another giant execution tranche instead of a decision brief; (b) a paperwork brief with no executed de-risking; (c) re-litigating the completed goal's claims instead of building on them
- Blind spots to consider: the fleet's actual day-one shape vs the proven matrix; the 5-of-6 pre-Ivy prevalence (most webpack-era Angular apps need the ngcc-bearing 12/13 cell, which is declared tranche-two); 50 of 58 capabilities are single-app experimental (cross-proving them is what widens honest support fastest); throughput/cost per app at fleet scale (the proven flow is deep but manual-ish); the fmt format epoch; test-infrastructure gaps found during the run (determinism-under-load refusal path lacks per-pass capture; witness runs must serialize)

## Owner Update (2026-08-14)

After reviewing the fleet day-one evidence, the owner ruled: **install+build of the migrated tree, Witness browser-parity proof, and ingest/identity/era-cell provisioning cannot be manual.** End-to-end automation of the per-app pipeline is a product requirement for fleet use, not an optimization. Consequences, board-encoded:

- The decision brief's how-to-proceed MUST center on closing these three manual gaps as product (CLI-driven, not fixture-code-driven), with the journey-authoring cost (the measured ~48% item) treated as the central engineering problem. Candidate mechanisms the brief must assess: journey synthesis from the app's own e2e suites (the cypress-rwa journey was derived from the app's own Cypress specs — a real precedent), generic crawl-based journey fallback, parameterized ingest over the existing tier-f machinery, era-cell provisioning as a CLI concern, and install/build execution folded into the migrate flow.
- Spikes A/B/C stay as specified — they MEASURE the automation gap precisely (machine-time vs authoring-time split, thin-wrapper floor, prune policy) and their numbers price the automation work.
- This does not authorize executing the automation inside this goal (the misfire clause stands); it authorizes ranking it as the requirement it is.

## Known Candidate Directions (Scout must evidence, not assume)

1. **Angular 12/13 ngcc-bearing multi-hop cell** — the declared tranche-two commitment; the mechanism serving the observed fleet shape (5-of-6 pre-Ivy prevalence). Cost: new cell readings, builder path, chase.
2. **Capability cross-proving campaign** — run fleet-shaped apps through the frozen adapters to promote experimental capabilities to cross-proven, widening the honest support matrix without reopening adapters.
3. **Fleet-scale operator throughput** — batch/parallel operator flows, cost-per-app measurement, failure triage UX; what 300+ apps actually need day one.
4. **React fleet depth** — more CRA/webpack-era React coverage (the fleet is ~half React; the React adapter is frozen-proven on 7 apps).
5. **Robustness/test infrastructure** — per-pass measurement capture on refusal paths, serialized witness scheduling, format epoch, CI.

The board must weigh these (and anything Scout finds) by: owner deadline impact, honest-support-widening per unit effort, risk of invalidating existing claims, and testing robustness.

## Goal Oracle

`A committed owner decision brief (docs + board note + final PM summary to the owner) in which: every candidate direction is assessed from primary evidence with explicit effort/impact/risk; the ranked top recommendation is de-risked by at least one executed Worker spike with canonical receipts; testing strategies are concrete (commands, gates, cadence); nothing contradicts or overclaims the completed goal's sealed receipts; and a final Judge audit maps every brief claim to evidence and records full_outcome_complete: true.`

## Non-Negotiable Constraints

- The completed goal's sealed receipts, freeze `27741d9c`, boundary declarations, and bounded outcome strings are inputs — never weakened, never restated more generally.
- Adapter reopens require the same authorized-reopen discipline as before (a spike may propose one; only the board authorizes it, and any reopen must end re-frozen).
- Worker dispatch goes through the fable-opus cockpit packet gate (`opus-worker` / `opus-worker-isolated`); the PM loads the cockpit skill before first dispatch and honors packet/ledger/breaker rules.
- Standing autonomy directive carries over (owner, 2026-08-10): no interruptions for orchestration-internal decisions; ledgered auto-continue on task-breaker latches; surface only genuinely owner-level decisions.
- Strict TypeScript, magic-regexp/pathe/ufo, local `@async/witness` via link:, offline-after-ingest, no payment data/credentials/host paths in evidence — all carried over.
- Spikes are bounded and reversible; a spike that grows into a tranche is a misfire — cut it and record what was learned.
- Commit each coherent verified slice.

## Stop Rule

Stop only when the final Judge maps the decision brief to its evidence and records `full_outcome_complete: true`, and the PM has surfaced the brief to the owner in plain language with the "how to proceed" options ranked.

Do not stop after discovery, after ranking, or after one spike while the brief is unwritten. Do not balloon into executing the chosen tranche — that is the next goal, started by the owner from the brief.

## Board Health

Machine truth lives in `docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/state.yaml`. Validate with the GoalBuddy checker before stopping any turn.

## Run Command

```text
/goal Follow docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/goal.md.
```

## PM Loop

1. Read this charter and `state.yaml`; work only the active task; one write Worker at a time.
2. Scout → Judge-ranked strategy → bounded de-risk spikes (cockpit-dispatched) → decision brief → final audit.
3. Compact receipts; commit coherent slices; continue immediately to the next safe task.
4. Complete only via the final Judge audit, then surface the brief to the owner.

4. **React fleet depth** — more CRA/webpack-era React coverage (the fleet is ~half React; the React adapter is frozen-proven on 7 apps).
5. **Robustness/test infrastructure** — per-pass measurement capture on refusal paths, serialized witness scheduling, format epoch, CI.

The board must weigh these (and anything Scout finds) by: owner deadline impact, honest-support-widening per unit effort, risk of invalidating existing claims, and testing robustness.

## Goal Oracle

`A committed owner decision brief (docs + board note + final PM summary to the owner) in which: every candidate direction is assessed from primary evidence with explicit effort/impact/risk; the ranked top recommendation is de-risked by at least one executed Worker spike with canonical receipts; testing strategies are concrete (commands, gates, cadence); nothing contradicts or overclaims the completed goal's sealed receipts; and a final Judge audit maps every brief claim to evidence and records full_outcome_complete: true.`

## Non-Negotiable Constraints

- The completed goal's sealed receipts, freeze `27741d9c`, boundary declarations, and bounded outcome strings are inputs — never weakened, never restated more generally.
- Adapter reopens require the same authorized-reopen discipline as before (a spike may propose one; only the board authorizes it, and any reopen must end re-frozen).
- Worker dispatch goes through the fable-opus cockpit packet gate (`opus-worker` / `opus-worker-isolated`); the PM loads the cockpit skill before first dispatch and honors packet/ledger/breaker rules.
- Standing autonomy directive carries over (owner, 2026-08-10): no interruptions for orchestration-internal decisions; ledgered auto-continue on task-breaker latches; surface only genuinely owner-level decisions.
- Strict TypeScript, magic-regexp/pathe/ufo, local `@async/witness` via link:, offline-after-ingest, no payment data/credentials/host paths in evidence — all carried over.
- Spikes are bounded and reversible; a spike that grows into a tranche is a misfire — cut it and record what was learned.
- Commit each coherent verified slice.

## Stop Rule

Stop only when the final Judge maps the decision brief to its evidence and records `full_outcome_complete: true`, and the PM has surfaced the brief to the owner in plain language with the "how to proceed" options ranked.

Do not stop after discovery, after ranking, or after one spike while the brief is unwritten. Do not balloon into executing the chosen tranche — that is the next goal, started by the owner from the brief.

## Board Health

Machine truth lives in `docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/state.yaml`. Validate with the GoalBuddy checker before stopping any turn.

## Run Command

```text
/goal Follow docs/goals/next-tranche-strategy/goal.md.
```

## PM Loop

1. Read this charter and `state.yaml`; work only the active task; one write Worker at a time.
2. Scout → Judge-ranked strategy → bounded de-risk spikes (cockpit-dispatched) → decision brief → final audit.
3. Compact receipts; commit coherent slices; continue immediately to the next safe task.
4. Complete only via the final Judge audit, then surface the brief to the owner.

content.content:
# T002 Dossier — Fleet Day-One Needs Map (operator's-eye view)

## 1. The per-app pipeline today (as the 12 corpus + 2 holdout apps were actually done)

| Step | Driven by | Per-app new TypeScript? | Practice cost (ledger evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Consented ingest + identity/license | **Fixture-code** — per-app `*-ingest.ts` in `packages/cli/src/fixture/` | Yes: ~670–1,570 lines each (e.g. `react-strapi-ingest.ts` 1,194; `react-actual-budget-v22-12-9-ingest.ts` 1,519). Batch screeners exist (`tier-f-ingest.ts` 3,240, `legacy-candidate-ingest.ts` 987) | Part of the ~3u/40min screen (lrapr-t018) |
| Era cell provisioning + baseline lanes | Fixture-code (per-app baseline runs) | Mostly reuse of framework machinery; per-app run files | Included in vertical cost; disk 0.5–1.3G cache per app |
| analyze / plan / migrate | **CLI** — `packages/cli/src/operator/` (5 commands, generic, offline) | **No** | Whole surface built in 2u/55min (lrapr-t009) |
| Migrated install/build | Fixture-code — per-app `*-run.ts` drivers (700–1,100 lines) | Yes | Machine time inside the 9–10u vertical |
| Witness journey authoring + calibration | **Hand-driven TS**: AppSpec/journey in `real-app-run.ts` (7,453-line generic harness) + per-app run file (235–544 lines) + projections (`memos-projection.ts` 1,011; `angular-eshop-webspa-projection.ts` 493; `papercups-projection.ts` 343) + calibrate fixtures (`react-cypress-rwa-calibrate-run.ts`, two super-productivity calibrate runs) | Yes — the dominant per-app authorship | **35 of 73 distinct units in lrapr-t006 are u19\*/u20\*** — journey authoring/calibration for just two Angular apps ≈ half a 30-hour tranche |
| Parity/determinism/mutation/locality gates | Generic runners invoked via per-app drivers | No new logic, but wired per app | 2+2 witness passes, double builds — serialized |
| Receipts/publish | **Hand-written per-app schema modules** in `packages/core/src/receipts/` | Yes: 41 files / 24,769 lines; per-app witness schemas 300–2,334 lines (`witness-angular-super-productivity.ts` 2,334; `witness-angular-tiny-translator.ts` 1,554) | Inside vertical cost |

Inventory: `packages/cli/src/fixture/` = **144 files / 79,726 lines**, overwhelmingly per-app; `packages/cli/src/witness/` = 30 files / 17,903 lines (~10k generic harness, rest per-app); `packages/core/src/receipts/` = 41 files / 24,769 lines. A full app today means ~4–6 new TS files, roughly 2,000–5,000 lines.

**Convergence already visible:** newest per-app witness wrappers are thin (`react-dejavu-run.ts` 61 lines, `angular-fuxa-run.ts` 67 lines vs tiny-translator's 544) because `real-app-run.ts` + `witness-real-app.ts` (1,116 lines) generalized. The amortization path exists; it isn't yet the default for receipts or ingest.

## 2. Expensive points, ranked

1. **Witness journey authoring/calibration** — 48% of the largest run's units (u19a–k tiny-translator, u20a–u20c2r super-productivity, incl. failed attempts like u19c "uncalibrated: no browser pass ran"). Measure-before-pin requires live serialized browser rounds. *Amortizer:* declarative AppSpec/journey format + a calibration harness generalizing the `react-cypress-rwa-calibrate-run.ts` pattern.
2. **Per-app receipt schema modules** — up to 2,334 hand lines/app. *Amortizer:* make `witness-real-app.ts` the default schema; per-app modules only for bounded-outcome apps.
3. **Ingest fixtures** — ~1,000 lines/app but template-shaped; *amortizer:* parameterized ingest over `tier-f-ingest.ts`/`legacy-candidate-ingest.ts` machinery.
4. **Projections** for backend-bearing apps (300–1,000 lines) — hardest to generate; `live-backend.ts` (376 lines, commit d7ebff6) is the generic seed.

## 3. Scale breaks N=10 → N=300

- **Disk breaks first**: `.versionless/cache` **20G** + `.versionless/work` **19G** ≈ 39G for ~14 apps ⇒ **~2.8G/app ⇒ ~840G–1TB at 300 apps** on one host (largest: sqlpad/cypress-rwa work 3.1G each; next-tailwind deps cache 7.1G). Needs a prune-after-receipt policy (ambiguity: is work/cache needed for offline verify? receipts suggest no — Judge/PM confirm).
- **Wall-clock second**: 9–10u/3–4h per green vertical ⇒ 300 apps ≈ **~1,050h ≈ 44 serial days** at today's cost — and the determinism-under-load finding (T010/T011: gates green serial, fail parallel) means **witness runs cannot parallelize on one host**; multi-host is the only witness-throughput lever, and the rate conflates authoring with machine time (pure machine time per already-supported app is unmeasured — a gap).
- **Era-cell reuse: none across apps** — caches are per-app-baseline keyed (`angular-jira-clone-baseline`, `react-hospitalrun-baseline`…); 300 apps duplicate toolchains.
- **Evidence repo third**: 478M, but 435M is one source-carrying ingest (`angular-eshop-webspa-netcore2-2`); typical ingest dirs are 100–400K. Fine at 300 apps **iff** sources are never vendored again.

## 4. Friction vs coverage — the clean split for the Judge

- **Friction reducers (apps already inside supported shapes):** Direction 3 (batch operator runner, 3–6u) + Direction 5's serialization-scheduler/CI slice + generic journey/receipt tooling (the dejavu/fuxa 60-line pattern industrialized). These could cut ~10u/app toward ~3u/app but add **zero** newly servable apps.
- **Coverage wideners (apps that can enter the pipeline at all):** Direction 1 (ngcc 12/13 cell) is the only mover — ~125 of ~150 Angular fleet apps (Wilson CI 65–145) are blocked at the pre-Ivy boundary; only ~25 servable today. Secondary limits: no React/Next target cell (analyze reports "no cell" — doesn't block CRA→Vite migration, the cross-proven dominant fleet shape), and identity/witness surface limits (live-backend/auth apps get bounded outcomes, eShop precedent).
- Directions 2/4 are **depth within existing coverage** (capability cross-proving), not friction or width.

## 5. Payment-adjacent apps

- **Mechanized:** `packages/core/src/policy/payment-signals.ts` (forbidden keys: pan/cvv/card/payment/account/token…; `sk_live|sk_test`, bearer, private-key regexes; PAN-like 13–19 digit detector) is wired into `packages/core/src/receipts/verify.ts` — every receipt verification runs the sensitive scan — and `packages/core/src/corpus/tier-f-provenance.ts`. Redaction is applied at capture in the generic witness harness (22 redact sites in `real-app-run.ts`). Charter makes payment data in evidence release-blocking (`legacy…/state.yaml:263,:1209,:1288`); T014 final audit recorded "redaction/payment gates clean."
- **Operator-manual residue:** the gates are artifact-side/post-hoc. Nothing stops an operator's authored journey from *entering* real payment data during a live pass; discipline lives in journey design (cypress-rwa, the payment-adjacent precedent, passed with synthetic data). No fleet-level pre-flight "payment-app mode" exists in the operator CLI.

# T004 / SPIKE B — batch operator dry run

Unit `nts-t004/spike-b-batch-operator-dryrun`. Measured 2026-08-14, offline, one host.

Primary evidence: `evidence/spikes/fleet-batch-dryrun/fleet-summary.json`,
`evidence/spikes/fleet-batch-dryrun/prune-safety.json`, human rendering
`evidence/spikes/fleet-batch-dryrun/README.md` (passed through
`assertEnterpriseSurfaceHonesty`). Driver:
`packages/cli/src/fixture/fleet-batch-spike-run.ts`. Test:
`packages/cli/test/fleet-batch-spike.test.ts`.

This spike closes two gaps T002 named: "pure machine time per already-supported
app is unmeasured — a gap", and the prune-policy ambiguity "is work/cache needed
for offline verify? receipts suggest no — Judge/PM confirm".

## What was run

The existing operator flows — `analyze`, `plan`, `migrate` from
`packages/cli/src/operator/flows.ts` — were looped over **12 already-ingested
application roots, 7 React and 5 Angular**, taken from work areas this checkout
already carried. Nothing was acquired, installed or built. The operator surface
was not modified; the driver composes it and adds no migration decision.

Read-only stages were timed three times each and reported as a median; the write
stage ran once per application into a fresh scratch lane under the OS temporary
directory, because the apply flow refuses a lane that already carries files.
Timing is `process.hrtime.bigint()` around the awaited call and nothing else — no
authoring inside any timed region.

Outcomes: **8 migrated into a scratch lane, 4 refused by name.** Both refusal
classes are real fleet shapes and both are quoted verbatim in the record: React
trees declaring neither react-scripts nor a Vite configuration (react-mycrypto,
react-boilerplate-v4), and Angular workspaces whose tsconfig carries comments
(angular-realworld-v15-to-v16, angular-realworld-production-parity).

## Finding 1 — operator machine time is not the bottleneck, by three orders of magnitude

| population | apps | per app (median) | per app (mean) | serial at N=300 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| measured fleet, every outcome | 12 | 0.80 ms | 13.43 ms | **4.0 s** |
| plan composed and migrated | 8 | 1.02 ms | 19.98 ms | 6.0 s |
| refused by the flows | 4 | 0.35 ms | 0.34 ms | 0.1 s |
| React lineage | 7 | 0.79 ms | 0.70 ms | 0.2 s |
| Angular lineage | 5 | 6.45 ms | 31.26 ms | 9.4 s |

Per stage: analyze 0.36 ms median (0.12 s at 300), plan 0.69 ms median (7.2 s at
300 on the mean), migrate 1.02 ms median (6.0 s at 300 on the mean). The whole
12-application loop took **0.81 s of wall clock**.

The stages are not additive — `plan` re-runs detection and `migrate` re-runs
detection and composition — so a per-application pass is costed at the deepest
stage that completed, not the row sum.

Lineage asymmetry is real and structural: Angular composition walks the workspace
(pigallery2 scans 175 files, ~105 ms) while the React hop writes one entry
document (~1 ms). Angular is roughly 40x React per pass and still negligible.

**Reading for the owner's end-to-end automation ruling.** The `analyze/plan/migrate`
third of the pipeline costs about **6 seconds of machine time for the entire
300-application fleet**. Automating it therefore buys essentially no machine time.
What it buys is the removal of per-app authoring and the ability to schedule
unattended — which is the whole of its value, and should be argued on that basis
rather than on throughput. The cost that remains after this work is done is the
unmeasured part: install, migrated build, and witness authoring/calibration/passes.

## Finding 2 — the work tree is prunable after receipt (verdict: yes)

Application `react-boilerplate-v4-composed`; receipt
`evidence/runs/react-boilerplate-v4-composed/t060-run.json` (the canonical default
`receipt:verify` target); work directory `.versionless/work/react-boilerplate-v4-composed`
(7,571,741 bytes).

`verifyReceipt(receipt, { requireAggregate: true })` — the same function
`versionless receipt:verify` calls — was run three times: with the directory
present, with it **renamed** to a sibling set-aside path (a move inside the same
unversioned scratch tree; nothing was deleted), and again after it was renamed
back. Absence was checked inside the middle window rather than assumed; the
restore ran in a `finally`; the restored listing was compared entry by entry.

All three returned `state: pass`, **10 artifacts, digest
`52400147929220935a9ebe47a16c8dff50b5c28e9d51c930d000c99c2bdc8a21` — identical
with the work directory absent as with it present.** Restored: true.

**Disk floor implication.** Measured separately on this checkout:
`.versionless/work` = **20.6 GB** and `.versionless/cache` = **21.3 GB** across 28
work areas (largest single work areas: react-sqlpad 3.29 GB, react-cypress-rwa
3.27 GB, angular-pigallery2 2.94 GB). T002's projection of ~840 GB–1 TB at 300
apps was built on that per-app footprint. Because the offline verification does
not resolve any path under the work tree, **the work tree can be pruned once the
receipt is published without losing the offline check**, and the disk floor at
N=300 is set by the evidence tree rather than the work tree. Re-migrating a pruned
application means re-acquiring its sources and era closure first.

Bounds on that verdict, carried in the record: it is proven on one receipt, and a
receipt schema that reads a lane out of `.versionless/work` would behave
differently and must be checked before the policy is applied to it. The directory
moved aside holds ~7.6 MB while the largest hold three orders of magnitude more —
the mechanism proven is path-independence, which does not depend on size, but this
is one directory rather than a survey. Note also that this spike proves nothing
about `.versionless/cache` (21.3 GB), which was not moved or tested.

## Finding 3 — what parallelizes, and what does not

Recorded in the summary as readings off what each flow does to disk, not as a
load measurement:

- **analyze** — parallelizable across processes; reads declarations, writes nothing.
- **plan** — parallelizable across processes; writes nothing into the tree it read.
- **migrate** — parallelizable across processes, one lane per application; the apply
  flow refuses a lane inside the application and refuses a non-empty lane, so
  concurrent migrations with distinct lanes cannot reach the same bytes.
- **witness browser passes** — **witness-serialized on one host**, per the
  determinism-under-load finding carried over from the previous goal (T010/T011:
  gates green serial, fail parallel). Multi-host remains the only witness
  throughput lever. No projection here assumes this stage parallelizes.
- **install and migrated build** — not measured; concurrency behaviour not established.

Since the three operator stages are already ~6 s for the whole fleet, parallelizing
them has no practical value. The parallelism finding matters only as a constraint
statement for the stages this spike did not measure.

# SPIKE C — the real per-application cost, measured on a never-completed application

Unit `nts-t004/spike-c-thin-wrapper-cost`. Measured 2026-08-14 on one host
(darwin-arm64, Node v24.15.0, npm 12.0.1). Machine record:
`evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json`.

The spike was sent to price the post-industrialization per-application cost by
taking a never-completed application through the frozen React adapter and
witnessing it through the thin-wrapper path. It did not get there. What follows
is what it did measure, and where it stopped.

## Gate zero — license text at the pin

Both candidates pass, read out of the consented archive already on disk after
that archive was re-verified against the digest its ingest recorded.

| application | pinned commit | license file | sha256 | gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| react-shlink-web-client | `44aca4ae` | `LICENSE` (MIT License) | `249a81967c48177d9fa4672adbfdecd356aba715101780e05d54fcbd744d699c` | pass |
| react-sqlpad-v5-5-0 | `5c259dd7` | `LICENSE.md` (#The MIT License) | `93dec0b7b1f9775cdcb15603a6c1d8829164ac72fa01a4679845c85ee76421da` | pass |

The primary passed, so no license fallback was taken. `react-sqlpad-v5-5-0` was
read only as a comparator.

## Where it stopped

Two walls, both before the stage the ~3u estimate describes.

**The frozen React adapter refuses the application.** `analyze` reads it as React
with builder `unknown`; `plan` and `migrate` both refuse:

> React plan: this tree declares neither react-scripts nor a Vite configuration, so no frozen React adapter claims it. This flow refuses rather than guessing an origin toolchain.

shlink-web-client v2.3.0 is an ejected create-react-app: it carries its own
webpack 4 configuration under `config/` and does not declare `react-scripts`.
This is a named gap. No frozen subtree was edited.

**The era cell refuses the baseline.** With one Node era cell installed on this
host, webpack 4 fails first on hashing —
`error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported` — which
`NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider` answers, and then the build stops for
good on the native dependency:

> ./src/common/react-tagsinput.scss — Error: Node Sass does not yet support your current environment: OS X Unsupported architecture (arm64) with Unsupported runtime (137)

The corpus source is immutable, so swapping node-sass for dart-sass is not
available, and no second era cell is installed.

## The ledger

| stage | machine | operator | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| license pre-screen (both) | 3 s | ~10 min | pass |
| ingest completion (both) | 2 s | ~2 min | source complete both; no dependency closure for the primary |
| baseline install | 20 s over 2 attempts | ~3 min | installed after one refusal (`EALLOWREMOTE`) and one operator decision (`--allow-remote all`) |
| baseline production build | 10 s over 2 attempts | ~4 min | not built |
| migrate under the frozen adapter | 1.04 s | ~2 min | refused |
| migrate, admitted comparator (sqlpad client) | 0.95 s | ~1 min | materialised: 1 file written, 167 copied |
| witness, thin-wrapper path | 0 | 0 | not executed |
| **total** | **37 s** | **~22 min** | **0 builds, 0 witness passes, 0 new TypeScript lines** |

Machine seconds are wall clock around the awaited command and nothing else.
Operator seconds are the acts between commands — reading a refusal, choosing a
remedy — and are never folded into machine time.

## What this says about ~3u per application

`threeUnitsCredible: false`, and the reason matters more than the flag: the
claim was not reached rather than refuted. An application drawn from the
never-completed set spent its whole budget on the stages *before* the one the
estimate covers. Any per-application average that quotes only the applications
that made it through is quoting a filtered population.

Four costs remain manual, and this run priced the first three:

1. **Era-cell provisioning** — two failed builds, ~4 minutes, no remedy on this host.
2. **Install policy** (remote tarballs, install scripts) — one failed install, ~3 minutes; both mechanisable as policy, both judgment today.
3. **Adapter admission** for trees outside the react-scripts/Vite declaration — ~2 minutes, then the application leaves the pipeline.
4. **The migrated tree is not yet installable from the CLI.** On the admitted comparator, `migrate --materialize` wrote one file (the entry document) and copied 167; the lane's `package.json` still declares `react-scripts ^3.4.1` and carries no Vite configuration. The Vite-era rewrite for the applications already completed lives in per-application fixture code (18 to 318 lines each).

Witness journey authoring and calibration were not touched here, so T002's
reading of that stage stands unrevised.

## The thin-wrapper floor, as inventory

The pattern this spike was sent to price is real on disk — `react-dejavu-run.ts`
is 61 lines and `angular-fuxa-run.ts` 67, over the 7,453-line generic harness,
against 235 to 436 lines for the earlier per-application wrappers. That is
inventory of work already done. It is not evidence that a new application
reaches that floor, because no new application here reached the stage where the
wrapper is written.

## Not established

- No build ran to completion, so nothing here establishes that either application builds on any era cell.
- No witness pass ran, so nothing here establishes browser behaviour, parity, locality, or a bounded witness outcome.
- The thin-wrapper line counts are inventory of previously completed applications, not a measurement of a new one.
- Operator timings are single-run wall clock on one host, not a distribution.
- The refusals are readings of this host and this pin; a different architecture, era cell, or npm would refuse differently, and none was tested.
- Nothing here revises the frozen adapters, the supported matrix, or any capability status; no coverage or matrix artifact was regenerated.

# T004 / SPIKE C — the real per-application cost, on a never-completed application

Unit `nts-t004/spike-c-thin-wrapper-cost`. Measured 2026-08-14, one host
(darwin-arm64, Node v24.15.0, npm 12.0.1), 60-minute wall-clock budget.

Primary evidence: `evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/verdict.json`; human
rendering `evidence/spikes/thin-wrapper-cost/README.md`; test
`packages/cli/test/thin-wrapper-cost-spike.test.ts`.

## What was asked and what happened

The spike was to price the post-industrialization per-application cost by taking
`react-shlink-web-client` (v2.3.0, an existing consented ingest never carried to
completion) through the frozen React adapter and witnessing it through the
thin-wrapper path, clocking each stage.

It never reached the migrated build, and therefore never reached the witness
wrapper the unit was named for. Two walls stopped it, and both are worth more to
the decision brief than the number the spike was sent to fetch would have been.

**Gate zero passed for both candidates.** shlink `LICENSE` at commit `44aca4ae`
is MIT, sha256 `249a81967c48177d9fa4672adbfdecd356aba715101780e05d54fcbd744d699c`;
sqlpad `LICENSE.md` at `5c259dd7` is MIT, sha256
`93dec0b7b1f9775cdcb15603a6c1d8829164ac72fa01a4679845c85ee76421da`. Both cached
archives re-verified byte-identical against their recorded ingest digests, so no
license fallback was taken and no acquisition endpoint was re-read.

## Finding C1 — the frozen React adapter refuses ejected create-react-app

`analyze` reads shlink as React with builder `unknown`; `plan` and `migrate`
both refuse with the adapter's own words:

> React plan: this tree declares neither react-scripts nor a Vite configuration, so no frozen React adapter claims it. This flow refuses rather than guessing an origin toolchain.

shlink v2.3.0 ejected: its webpack 4 configuration is vendored under `config/`
and `react-scripts` is not declared. This is the same refusal class Spike B saw
on react-mycrypto and react-boilerplate-v4 — but those were already-processed
work areas, and this is a fresh application drawn from the never-completed set,
which makes the class a **fleet admission limit** rather than a curiosity.
Ejected CRA is a mainstream webpack-era React shape. Named gap; no frozen
subtree was edited (freeze recompute unchanged).

## Finding C2 — the era cell, not the migration, ends the baseline

With one Node era cell on the host, the baseline build fails twice: webpack 4's
md4 hashing (`error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported`), answered
by `NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider`, and then terminally on the native
dependency:

> ./src/common/react-tagsinput.scss — Error: Node Sass does not yet support your current environment: OS X Unsupported architecture (arm64) with Unsupported runtime (137)

node-sass 4.x publishes no arm64 binding for a modern Node ABI; the corpus
source is immutable, so a dart-sass swap is not available; and installing an
older era cell is a network act outside this unit's consent. **The application's
own baseline cannot be reproduced on this host at all.** For the brief: era-cell
provisioning is not merely "manual", it is sometimes *impossible* on a
single-architecture host, and that is a fleet-planning input (architecture of
the runner pool), not only an automation task.

## Finding C3 — modern npm adds two per-application judgment calls

`npm ci` refuses the 2020 lockfile outright (`EALLOWREMOTE`, on a dependency
pinned to an https tarball at registry.yarnpkg.com) until `--allow-remote all`
is passed; and install scripts are skipped by default, which silently produced a
tree whose native dependency was never built — the reason the failure surfaced at
build time rather than install time. Both are mechanisable as fleet policy; both
are unwritten judgment today.

## Finding C4 — `migrate` emits an entry document, not an installable tree

Measured on the admitted comparator (`react-sqlpad-v5-5-0`'s `client/`, which the
adapter *does* claim): `migrate --out <lane> --materialize` completes in 0.34 s
and records **1 file written (`index.html`), 167 copied, 0 removed** — and the
lane's `package.json` still declares `react-scripts ^3.4.1` with no Vite
configuration. The Vite-era rewrite for the applications already completed lives
in per-application fixture code (`react-linkfree-v0-72-0-vite8.ts` 318 lines,
`react-hospitalrun-vite8.ts` 272, `react-memos-v0-1-3-vite8-run.ts` 255,
`react-avataaars-vite8.config.ts` 18).

This is the sharpest input to the owner's ruling that install+build of the
migrated tree cannot be manual: **today it cannot be automated from the CLI at
all**, because the CLI does not yet emit a tree that installs. That is a product
gap in `migrate`, not an operator habit.

## The ledger

| stage | machine | operator | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| license pre-screen (both candidates) | 3 s | ~10 min | pass |
| ingest completion (both) | 2 s | ~2 min | source complete both; primary has no dependency closure (T712/T714 both ended permanent-exclusion) |
| baseline install | 20 s / 2 attempts | ~3 min | installed after one refusal and one decision |
| baseline production build | 10 s / 2 attempts | ~4 min | **not built** |
| migrate under the frozen adapter | 1.04 s | ~2 min | **refused** |
| migrate, admitted comparator | 0.95 s | ~1 min | materialised (1 written, 167 copied) |
| witness via thin wrapper | 0 | 0 | **not executed** |
| total | **37 s** | **~22 min** | 0 builds, 0 witness passes, **0 new TypeScript lines** |

Machine seconds are wall clock around the awaited command; operator seconds are
the acts between commands and are never folded into machine time.

## Verdict — `threeUnitsCredible: false`, and why the reason matters

The ~3u/app reading is **not established, and not refuted**: the application
spent its entire budget on stages *before* the one the estimate describes. The
honest form for the brief is:

> A per-application average taken over applications that completed is an average over a filtered population. This spike drew one application from the unfiltered set and it did not enter the pipeline — the frozen adapter did not claim it, and its own baseline would not build on the only era cell available.

For the brief's ranking, the practical consequence is that the automation work
the owner ruled a product requirement has a prerequisite this spike surfaced:
**admission and era-cell provisioning decide whether an application has a
per-application cost at all.** Industrializing the witness/receipt/ingest
stages reduces the cost of applications already inside the boundary; it does not
move the boundary. Direction 1 (coverage width) and an admission widening for
ejected-CRA/webpack-era React trees are what move it.

The thin-wrapper floor itself remains as inventory only: `react-dejavu-run.ts`
61 lines and `angular-fuxa-run.ts` 67 over the 7,453-line generic harness,
against 235–436 lines for the earlier per-application wrappers. No new
application reached the stage where that file is written, so the floor is
unproven for a new application, and no per-application module under
`packages/core/src/receipts` was written or shown to be needed.

## Bounds

One host, one pin, one attempt per stage; single-run wall clock, not a
distribution. No build completed and no witness pass ran, so nothing here
establishes build, browser, parity, locality, or capability behaviour for either
application. Nothing was regenerated — no coverage, matrix, or enterprise-report
artifact was touched — and the freeze composite is unchanged.
